title: Cartesian geometric descent and effective groupoids in spaces
statement: Use the spaces, universes and coherent diagrams of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. For a small simplicial space $X_\bullet$ write $|X_\bullet|=\operatorname{colim}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}X_n$. The map $X_0\to|X_\bullet|$ is surjective on $\pi_0$. Geometric realization commutes with finite products of simplicial spaces. If a natural transformation $Y_\bullet\to X_\bullet$ has a pullback naturality square for every arrow of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, then $Y_n\to|Y_\bullet|$ over $X_n\to|X_\bullet|$ is a pullback square for each $n$. For a nonempty ordered subset $S\subseteq[n]$, write $G_S=G_{|S|-1}$ with restriction induced by increasing enumeration. A simplicial space $G_\bullet$ is called a groupoid object if, for every union $[n]=S\cup T$ with one common vertex, its restriction map $G_n\to G_S\times_{G_{S\cap T}}G_T$ is an equivalence. Every groupoid object in spaces is effective: its augmentation $G_0\to|G_\bullet|$ is surjective on $\pi_0$, and $G_n\simeq G_0\times_{|G_\bullet|}\cdots\times_{|G_\bullet|}G_0$ with $n+1$ factors, naturally with the simplicial operators. In particular $G_1\simeq G_0\times_{|G_\bullet|}G_0$. For a commutative square $Y\to Y\prime$ over $X\to X\prime$, let $q:Y\to X\times_{X\prime}Y\prime$ be its pullback comparison. If $T\to X$ is surjective on $\pi_0$ and $q$ is an equivalence on every homotopy fiber over every point of $T$, then $q$ is an equivalence.
